name: S-Class Omdura
body:
What Are S-Class Characters?

S-class characters are a request from Kenneth Zike. They are built using the summoner class, as originally presented, as the basis against which all other classes are balanced. The “S” in this case stands for both summoner and, as a more appropriate in-world reference, superior. If you have played—or GM’d for—a summoner and felt it was fine as is, you should have no problem running with an s-class character.

S-class omduras take faith in their gods’ plans, acting as the eyes and ears of their religion. The power that flows through them is shared with the worthy, and the wrath of the divine is felt by those who oppose and betray the omdura’s beliefs.

Role: S-class omduras can restore a fallen ally, then step in for them to help bring a decisive end to the conflict they face. They can be a spiritual leader, a capable soldier of their faith, and a pragmatic healer when the need arises.

Note: The s-class omdura is an alternate, superior version of the omdura class. When selecting archetypes, you choulse check to determine if any of those abilities are already changed by your choice of doctrine.

Alignment: An s-class omdura’s alignment must be within one step of their deity.

Hit Die: d8.

Parent Classes: Inquisitor and paladin.

Starting Wealth: 4d6 × 10 gp (average 140 gp.) In addition, an s-class omdura begins play with an outfit worth 10 gp or less.

Class Skills

The s-class omdura’s class skills are Appraise (Int), Bluff (Cha), Craft (Int), Diplomacy (Cha), Heal (Wis), Intimidate (Cha), Knowledge (arcana) (Int), Knowledge (nobility) (Int), Knowledge (planes) (Int), Knowledge (religion) (Int), Linguistics (Int), Perception (Wis), Profession (Wis), Sense Motive (Wis), and Spellcraft (Int).

Skill Ranks per Level: 4 + Int modifier.

Class Features

All of the following are class features of the s-class omdura.

Weapon and Armor Proficiency

An s-class omdura is proficient with all simple weapons and the favored weapon of their deity. They are also proficient with light armor, medium armor, and shields (except tower shields).

Aura

An s-class omdura of a chaotic, evil, good, or lawful deity has a powerful aura corresponding to the deity’s alignment (see the detect evil spell for details).

Spellcasting

An s-class omdura casts divine spells drawn from the cleric and inquisitor spell lists. Only cleric spells of 6th level and lower and inquisitor spells are considered to be part of the omdura spell list. If a spell appears on both the cleric and inquisitor spell lists, the omdura uses the lower of the two spell levels given for the spell. For instance, dimensional anchor is a 4th-level cleric spell and a 3rd-level inquisitor spell, which means it is a 3rd-level omdura spell.

The omdura can cast any spell they knows without preparing it ahead of time. To learn or cast a spell, an s-class omdura must have a Charisma score equal to at least 10 + the spell’s level. The difficulty class for a saving throw against an s-class omdura’s spell is 10 + the spell’s level + the omdura’s Charisma modifier.

An s-class omdura cannot use spell completion or spell trigger magic items of cleric spells of 7th level or higher (without a successful Use Magic Device check). Their alignment may restrict them from casting certain spells opposed to their moral or ethical beliefs; see Chaotic, Evil, Good, and Lawful Spells.

Like other spellcasters, an s-class omdura can cast only a certain number of spells of each spell level per day. Their base daily spell allotment is given on Table: S-Class Omdura. In addition, they receive bonus spells per day if they have a high Charisma score.

Unlike for clerics, an s-class omdura’s selection of spells is extremely limited. An s-class omdura begins play knowing four 0-level spells and two 1st-level spells of their choice. At each new omdura level, they learn one or more new spells, as indicated on Table: S-Class Omdura Spells Known. Unlike spells per day, the number of spells an s-class omdura knows is not affected by their Charisma score; the numbers on the table are fixed.

At 5th level and every 3 levels thereafter, an s-class omdura can learn a new spell in place of one they already know. In effect, the omdura loses the old spell in exchange for the new one. The new spell’s level must be the same as that of the spell being exchanged. An s-class omdura can swap only a single spell at any given level, and they must choose whether or not to swap the spell at the same time that they gains new spells known for the level. They cannot swap any cure or inflict spells.

Unlike a cleric, an s-class omdura need not prepare their spells in advance. They can cast any spell they knows at any time, assuming they has not yet used up their spells per day for that spell level.

Cure/Inflict: In addition to the spells gained as they gain levels, each omdura also adds all of either the cure spells or the inflict spells to their list of spells known (cure spells include all spells with “cure” in the name; inflict spells include all spells with “inflict” in the name). These spells are added as soon as the omdura is capable of casting them. A good omdura (or a neutral omdura of a good deity) must select cure spells. An evil omdura (or a neutral omdura of an evil deity) must select inflict spells. An s-class omdura who is neither good nor evil and whose deity is neither good nor evil can select either cure spells or inflict spells. This choice is made when the omdura gains their 1st level and cannot be changed.

Orisons: S-class omduras learn a number of orisons, or 0-level spells. These spells are cast like any other spell, but they do not consume spell slots and can be cast again. S-class omduras do not need to provide a divine focus to cast spells that list divine focus (DF) as part of the components.

Chaotic, Evil, Good, and Lawful Spells: An s-class omdura can’t cast spells of an alignment opposed to their own or their deity’s (if they has one). Spells associated with particular alignments are indicated by the chaos, evil, good, and law descriptors in their spell descriptions.

Detect Alignment (Sp)

At will, an s-class omdura can use detect chaos, detect evil, detect good, or detect law. They can only use one of these at any given time.

Doctrine

Each s-class omdura begins play with a doctrine; a line of teaching they follow that can change and influence some of their abilities as they gain experience. The doctrines presented at the end of this section are the champion, the self-reliant, and the unaligned.

Invocation (Su)

Starting at 1st level, an s-class omdura can invoke their deity’s divine will upon their allies within 30 feet as a standard action. The omdura does not receive their own bonus or special ability based on the type of invocation made.

An s-class omdura can use this ability for a number of minutes per day equal to their omdura level. The duration need not bee consecutive, but it must be spent in 1-minute increments. Once activated, this ability lasts until the combat ends, or until the omdura is killed, paralyzed, stunned, or knocked unconscious, at which point all of the bonuses immediately end.

When the omdura uses this ability, they must select one type of invocation. As a swift action, they can spend a 1-minute increment to change their invocation to another type. If the omdura is evil, they receive profane bonuses instead of sacred, as appropriate. Neutral omduras must select profane or sacred bonuses. Once made, this choice cannot be changed.

At 7th level, an s-class omdura can call an invocation as a move action instead of a standard action. At 13th level, an s-class omdura can call an invocation as a swift action.

At 11th level, when using their invocation class ability, the omdura chooses two invocations to grant their allies. In addition, the omdura now also benefits from any one invocation they use, but they receive only half of that invocation’s granted bonus.

At 20th level, each day when the omdura regains their spell slots, they choose one invocation to be active on themselves and their allies for the entire day. The omdura receives the full bonus granted by this invocation in addition to the half bonus they receive at 11th level and above.

For ease of reference, here are three invocations the omdura can use, and more are available to choose from in the original source. The GM can also provide additional invocations by modifying inquisitor judgments using these as guidelines.

Destruction: The omdura’s allies are filled with divine wrath, gaining a +1 sacred bonus on weapon damage rolls. This bonus increases by 1 for every 3 class levels the omdura has.

Resistance: The omdura’s allies are shielded by a flickering aura, gaining 2 points of energy resistance against one energy type (acid, cold, electricity, fire, or sonic)chosen when the omdura calls this invocation. The protection increases by 2 for every 3 class levels the omdura has.

Smiting: This invocation bathes the weapons of the omdura’s allies in a divine light. These weapons count as magic for the purpose of bypassing damage reduction. At 6th level, the allies’ weapons also count as one alignment type (chaotic, evil, good, or lawful) for the purpose of bypassing damage reduction. The type selected must match one of the omdura’s alignments. If the omdura is neutral, they do not grant this bonus. At 10th level, the allies’ weapons also count as adamantine for the purpose of overcoming damage reduction (but not for reducing hardness).

Divine Touch (Ex)

Beginning at 2nd level, an s-class omdura can heal wounds (their own or those of others) by touch. Evil omduras can choose instead to deal negative energy damage. Neutral omduras choose which to use, but once that choice is made, it cannot be changed.

Each day the omdurat can use this ability a number of times equal to 1/2 their omdura level plus their Charisma modifier. With one use of this ability, an s-class omdura can deal or restore 1d6 hit points of damage for every two omdura levels they possess. Using this ability is a standard action, unless the omdura targets themselves, in which case it is a swift action.

When an s-class omdura uses this power to damage creatures, they deal 1d6 points of damage for every two levels they possess. Using divine touch in this way requires a successful melee touch attack and doesn’t provoke an attack of opportunity. Creatures do not receive a saving throw against this damage.

Divine touch is modified by any feat, spell, or effect that specifically works with the lay on hands paladin class feature. For example, the Extra Lay On Hands feat grants an s-class omdura two additional uses of the divine touch class feature.

Divine Infusion (Su)

At 3rd level and every 3 levels thereafter, an s-class omdura can select one paladin mercy (if they are good), or one antipaladin cruelty (if they are evil) to apply when using divine touch. Neutral omduras gain either, depending on if they choose to channel positive or negative energy. At 6th, 9th, and 12th level, the omdura adds infusions to the list of those they can select as though they were a paladin or antipaladin (depending on their divine touch ability) of their omdura level.

Divine Might (Su)

At 4th level, an s-class omdura can call on the powers of their god once per day to aid in their struggle against their enemies. As a swift action, the omdura chooses one target within sight to be the focus of their divine might. If the target is opposed to the omdura’s alignment on either the law/chaos or the good/evil axis, the omdura adds half their Charisma bonus (minimum +o) to their attack rolls and adds half their omdura level to damage rolls against the target of their divine might. A neutral omdura can choose any target to be the target of their divine might, but they adds only one third their Charisma bonus and omdura level.

In addition, while divine might is in effect, the omdura gains a deflection bonus equal to half their Charisma modifier (one?third for a neutral omdura) to their AC against attacks made by the target of the divine might. If a non neutral omdura targets a creature that is not opposed to their alignment, the use of this ability is wasted with no effect.

At 18th level, the omdura uses their full Charisma bonus and full omdura level when using their divine might ability. A neutral omdura uses their full Charisma bonus and their omdura level – 3 when using their divine might ability.

The divine might effect remains until the target of divine might is dead or the next time the omdura rests and regains their uses of this ability. At 9th level and every 5 levels thereafter, the omdura can use divine might one additional time per day to a maximum of four times per day at 19th level.

Divine Weapon (Su)

At 5th level, an s-class omdura forms a divine bond with their god. This bond allows the omdura to enhance their weapon as a standard action by calling upon the aid of a divine spirit. This aid lasts for 1 minute per omdura level. When called, the spirit causes the weapon to shed light as a torch. At 5th level, this spirit grants the weapon a +1 enhancement bonus. For every 3 levels beyond 5th, the weapon gains another +1 enhancement bonus, to a maximum of +6 at 20th level. These bonuses can be added to the weapon, stacking with existing weapon bonuses to a maximum of +5, or they can be used to add any of the following weapon special abilities:

Alignment	Weapon Special Abilities
Any	brilliant energy, defending, flaming, flaming burst, keen, speed
Chaotic	anarchic, vicious
Evil	unholy, wounding
Good	disruption, holy
Lawful	axiomatic, merciful
Neutral	vorpal

Adding a special ability consumes an amount of bonus equal to the special ability’s cost (see Table: Melee Weapon Special Abilities). These bonuses are in addition to any special abilities the weapon already has, but duplicate abilities do not stack. If the weapon is not magic, at least a +1 enhancement bonus must be added before any other special abilities can be added. The bonus and special abilities granted by the spirit are determined when the spirit is called and cannot be changed until the spirit is called again. The divine spirit imparts no bonuses if the weapon is held by anyone other than the omdura, but it resumes granting bonuses if the weapon is returned to the omdura. These bonuses apply to only one end of a double weapon.

An s-class omdura can use this ability once per day at 5th level, and one additional time per day for every 4 levels beyond 5th, to a total of four times per day at 17th level.

If a weapon bonded with a divine spirit is destroyed, the omdura loses the use of this ability for 30 days or until they gains a level, whichever comes first. During this 30-day period, the omdura takes a-1 penalty on weapon attack and damage rolls.

Commune (Sp)

At 7th level, an s-class omdura can cast commune once per day as a spell-like ability. They can cast this a second time per day at 15th level.

Doctrines

Each of the doctrines below are available to s-class omduras.

Champion

S-class omdura champions lean more into their paladin training, which makes them more capable in direct combat at the cost of direct spellcasting.

Hit Dice and Base Attack Bonus

A champion’s hit die is a d10, and their base attack bonus is equal to their omdura level.

Spellcasting

Champions don’t gain omdura spellcasting.

Divine Might (Su)

A champion gains divine might once per day at 1st level. They can use divine might additional times per day starting at 9th level, as indicated on Table: S-Class Omdura.

Infusions (Su)

S-class omdura champions gain their first infusion at 2nd level. They gain additional infusions at 3rd level, and every 3 levels thereafter.

Bonus Feats

At 4th level, the champion gains a bonus feat. This feat can be chosen from any combat feat or teamwork feat. The champion must meet the prerequisites for these feats.

Tactician (Ex)

Also at 4th level, the champion gains a bonus teamwork feat. As a standard action, the champion can grant the benefits of one of their teamwork feats to all allies within 30 feet who can see and hear them. Allies retain the use of this bonus feat for 3 rounds plus 1 round for every two omdura levels the champion possesses. Allies do not need to meet the prerequisites of these bonus feats. The champion can use this ability once per day at 4th level, plus one additional time per day at 5th level and for every 5 levels thereafter.

Self-Reliant

Self-reliant omduras have adapted to working alone or in situations where they can only depend on their own talents to survive.

Heavy Armor Proficiency

Self-reliant omduras are proficient with heavy armor.

Solo Tactics (Ex)

At 3rd level, all of the self-reliant’s allies are treated as if they possessed the same teamwork feats as the self-reliant for the purpose of determining whether the self-reliant receives a bonus from their teamwork feats. Their allies do not receive any bonuses from these feats unless they actually possess the feats themselves. The allies’ positioning and actions must still meet the prerequisites listed in the teamwork feat for the self-reliant to receive the listed bonus.

Teamwork Feats

At 3rd level, and every three levels thereafter, the self-reliant gains a bonus feat in addition to those gained from normal advancement. These bonus feats must be selected from those listed as teamwork feats. The self-reliant must meet the prerequisites of the selected bonus feat.

As a standard action, the self-reliant can choose to learn a new bonus teamwork feat in place of the most recent bonus teamwork feat they have already learned. In effect, the self-reliant loses the bonus feat in exchange for the new one. They can only change the most recent teamwork feat gained. Whenever they gain a new teamwork feat, the previous teamwork feat becomes set and cannot be changed again. An s-class self-reliant can change their most recent teamwork feat a number of times per day equal to their Charisma modifier.

Commune (Sp)

A self-reliant can cast commune once per day at 7th level, plus one additional time per day at 13th and 19th level.

Unaligned

The unaligned are omduras whose power can be dispensed equally between their allies and their enemies. They are not bound by the same restrictions as clerics and other omduras.

Cure/Inflict

In addition to the spells gained as they gain levels, each unaligned also adds all cure spells and inflict spells to their list of spells known (cure spells include all spells with “cure” in the name; inflict spells include all spells with “inflict” in the name). These spells are added as soon as the omdura is capable of casting them.

Divine Touch (Su)

At 2nd level, the unaligned can use divine touch a number of times per day equal to their level plus their Charisma modifier. Each time they use divine touch, the unaligned chooses whether to channel positive or negative energy.

Infusions (Su)

Starting at 3rd level, when the unaligned gains an infusion, they choose one mercy and one cruelty. They apply mercies any time they heal a creature with divine touch, and cruelties any time they damage a creature with divine touch.

Divine Might (Su)

At 4th level, an unaligned can target any creature with divine might, regardless of that creature’s alignment.

Standard Omdura Doctrines

These doctrines are available to standard omduras as archetypes.

Champion Doctrine (Archetype)
Spellcasting

Champions don’t gain omdura spellcasting.

Divine Might (Su)

A champion gains divine might once per day at 1st level. They can use divine might additional times per day starting at 9th level, as indicated on Table: S-Class Omdura.

Invoke Might (Su)

When a champion uses invocation, they also treat their base attack bonus as equal to their omdura level for the duration. This may grant the champion additional attacks for having a high attack bonus.

Infusions (Su)

S-class omdura champions gain their first infusion at 2nd level. They gain additional infusions at 3rd level, and every 3 levels thereafter.

Bonus Feats

At 4th level, the champion gains a bonus feat. This feat can be chosen from any combat feat or teamwork feat. The champion must meet the prerequisites for these feats.

Tactician (Ex)

Also at 4th level, the champion gains a bonus teamwork feat. As a standard action, the champion can grant the benefits of one of their teamwork feats to all allies within 30 feet who can see and hear them. Allies retain the use of this bonus feat for 3 rounds plus 1 round for every two omdura levels the champion possesses. Allies do not need to meet the prerequisites of these bonus feats. The champion can use this ability once per day at 4th level, plus one additional time per day at 5th level and for every 5 levels thereafter.

Self-Reliant Doctrine (Archetype)
Skill Ranks per Level

A self-reliant gains 2 + Int modifier skill ranks per level.

Heavy Armor Proficiency

Self-reliant omduras are proficient with heavy armor.

Augury (Sp)

At 5th level, a self-reliant can cast augury as a spell-like ability once per day. They can cast it additional times per day at 9th, 13th, and 17th level.

This replaces the commune ability usually gained at 7th and 15th level.

Solo Tactics (Ex)

At 3rd level, all of the self-reliant’s allies are treated as if they possessed the same teamwork feats as the self-reliant for the purpose of determining whether the self-reliant receives a bonus from their teamwork feats. Their allies do not receive any bonuses from these feats unless they actually possess the feats themselves. The allies’ positioning and actions must still meet the prerequisites listed in the teamwork feat for the self-reliant to receive the listed bonus.

Teamwork Feats

At 3rd level, and every three levels thereafter, the self-reliant gains a bonus feat in addition to those gained from normal advancement. These bonus feats must be selected from those listed as teamwork feats. The self-reliant must meet the prerequisites of the selected bonus feat.

As a standard action, the self-reliant can choose to learn a new bonus teamwork feat in place of the most recent bonus teamwork feat they have already learned. In effect, the self-reliant loses the bonus feat in exchange for the new one. They can only change the most recent teamwork feat gained. Whenever they gain a new teamwork feat, the previous teamwork feat becomes set and cannot be changed again. An s-class self-reliant can change their most recent teamwork feat a number of times per day equal to their Charisma modifier.

Commune (Sp)

A self-reliant can cast commune once per day at 7th level, plus one additional time per day at 13th and 19th level.

Unaligned Doctrine (Archetype)
Skill Ranks per Level

An unaligned gains 2 + Int modifier skill ranks per level.

Detect Alignment (Sp)

Unaligned omduras do not gain this ability.

Cure/Inflict

In addition to the spells gained as they gain levels, each unaligned also adds all cure spells and inflict spells to their list of spells known (cure spells include all spells with “cure” in the name; inflict spells include all spells with “inflict” in the name). These spells are added as soon as the omdura is capable of casting them.

Divine Touch (Su)

At 2nd level, the unaligned can use divine touch a number of times per day equal to their level plus their Charisma modifier. Each time they use divine touch, the unaligned chooses whether to channel positive or negative energy.

S-Class Omdura Spell Suggestions

The following is a list of suggested spells for easy reference while playing an s-class omdura. These spells are intentionally summarized here. If you would like to see the full rules for these spells, including at which levels other classes gain them, please refer to the individual resources.

0-Level: acid splash, bleed, brand, daze, disrupt undead, stabilize

1st-Level: cause fear, cure light wounds, detect thoughts, disguise self, inflict light wounds, resist energy

2nd-Level: align weapon, cure moderate wounds, heroism, hold person, invisibility, protection from energy

3rd-Level: battle trance, cure serious wounds, dispel magic, fear, greater invisibility, remove curse, remove disease

4th-Level: break enchantment, cure critical wounds, greater brand, forced repentence, hold monster, legend lore

5th-Level: atonement, banishment, disrupting weapon, divine pursuit, spell resistance

6th-Level: blasphemy, dictum, forbiddance, heal, holy word, undeath to death, word of chaos

Infusions (Su)

Starting at 3rd level, when the unaligned gains an infusion, they choose one mercy and one cruelty. They apply mercies any time they heal a creature with divine touch, and cruelties any time they damage a creature with divine touch.

Divine Might (Su)

At 4th level, an unaligned can target any creature with divine might, regardless of that creature’s alignment.

Commune (Sp)

An unaligned gains this ability once per day at 7th level. they do not gain a second use per day.
